# 1 Clement Chapter 16 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 16 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_016_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 16

**16:1** Christ is with the humble-minded — not with those who lord it over his flock.

**16:2** The Lord Jesus Christ, the scepter of God's majesty, did not arrive with fanfare or arrogance — though he certainly could have. He came in humility of mind, just as the Holy Spirit said in advance about him:

**16:3** "Lord, who believed what we heard? Who saw God's powerful arm at work? We announced him like a baby, like a root pushing up from dry ground. He had no impressive form or glory. When we saw him, there was nothing beautiful about him — no majesty at all. He was looked down on, less than human, a man who suffered and knew sickness well, a man whose face people turned away from. He was despised, and nobody gave him a second thought." [Isa 53:1-3]

**16:4** "He carried our diseases and bore our suffering — but we thought he was being punished, afflicted by God." [Isa 53:4]

**16:5** "He was pierced for our rebellions, crushed for our sins. The punishment that gave us peace fell on him. His wounds are what healed us." [Isa 53:5]

**16:6** "All of us wandered off like sheep, each going our own way — and the Lord laid on him the guilt of us all." [Isa 53:6]

**16:7** "Because he was beaten down, he never opened his mouth. He was led like a sheep to slaughter; like a lamb silent before its shearer, he said nothing." [Isa 53:7]

**16:8** "By oppression and judgment he was taken away. Who can speak of his descendants? For he was cut off from the land of the living." [Isa 53:8]

**16:9** "It was for the sins of my people that he was struck." [Isa 53:8b]

**16:10** "He was buried with the wicked, with the rich in his death — though he had done nothing violent, and no lie was ever on his lips." [Isa 53:9]

**16:11** "Yet the LORD chose to crush him; it was the LORD's will to wound him. If he gives his life as a guilt offering, he will see his offspring and prolong his days." [Isa 53:10]

**16:12** "Out of the suffering of his soul he will see light and be satisfied. By his knowledge my righteous servant will justify many, and he will take on their guilt." [Isa 53:11]

**16:13** "Therefore I will give him a portion among the great, and he will divide the spoils with the strong — because he poured out his life unto death, and was counted with the rebels. He bore the sin of many and made intercession for the transgressors." [Isa 53:12]

**16:14** And in another place, speaking in his own person, he says: "I am a worm, not a man — mocked by all, despised by the people. Everyone who sees me laughs at me. They curl their lips and shake their heads: 'He trusted in God — let God rescue him! Let God save him — since God delights in him!'" [Ps 22:6-8]

**16:15** Do you see, beloved, what example is set before us? If the Lord himself was so humble in spirit, what should we be doing — we who came to him and live under the yoke of his grace?

---

*PNEUMA renders Isaiah 53 with full rhetorical power. This is the christological heart of the letter.*
